definition: A theoretical result stating that a neural network with at least one hidden layer and a sufficient number of neurons can approximate any continuous function to arbitrary accuracy.
details: The universal approximation theorem provides theoretical justification for why neural networks are such flexible function approximators, though it says nothing about how easy such functions are to actually learn via gradient-based training.
